title: Deterministic Verification and a Single-Repair Guardrail for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: a Paired, Shared‑Candidate Study
abstract: We report a sealed, preregistered paired experiment that measured the marginal verifier-detected effect of interposing a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair on the same LLM-generated configuration candidate. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (exactly one initial generation call per intent; that identical candidate reused for both baseline and guarded episodes) we generated one candidate per natural-language intent with gpt-5-mini for N = 250 pairs and evaluated two episodes per intent: baseline (accept candidate) and guarded (deterministic_netops_validator_v5; if failing, permit one automated repair). Execution completed 500 episodes with model_calls_used = 251. Results: baseline verifier-pass 249/250 (99.6%), guarded verifier-pass 250/250 (100.0%); contingency n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = +0.4 percentage points, 95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp] (paired bootstrap percentile, 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729), exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The single discordant pair was converted to pass by the single permitted repair. Important scope note (preregistered contrast not executed): the preregistered sim‑to‑real/production-like confirmatory comparison was not executed; the confirmatory estimand and numerical inference reported here apply only to the synthetic/emulation partition actually run. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are being explored as intent-to-configuration translators in network operations (NetOps), promising faster authoring of device CLI sequences and intent-driven automation. Stochastic generation, however, creates operational risk: syntax errors, incorrect command ordering, local-policy violations, and vendor-CLI subtleties can produce unsafe or non-functional device changes. Prior empirical and survey work documents LLM feasibility for draft configurations while highlighting the continuing need for deterministic verification or human oversight [1],[2].

A widely adopted architectural response is to interpose a deterministic validator between generation and acceptance, optionally followed by bounded automated repair — a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pattern — which accepts only validator-passed candidates or attempts limited repair when mechanically verifiable defects are detected [3],[5]. These pipelines demonstrably reduce mechanically verifiable error classes (syntax, simple ordering and local-policy violations), but open questions remain about the marginal benefit of such guardrails when modern LLM outputs already conform to validator encodings under constrained task regimes.

This paper reports a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment that isolates the marginal verifier+single-repair effect when the same initial candidate is reused across conditions (shared_initial_candidate semantics). By design the experiment measures only the validator-and-repair marginal effect on identical model outputs rather than conflating generation variability across conditions. Our principal contribution is the concrete, artifact-grounded quantification of that marginal effect and its statistical bounds for a constrained NetOps task set.
sections.related_work: Surveys and targeted studies motivate GVR architectures and verifier use in NetOps. Empirical work shows LLMs can produce draft configurations in controlled settings and that combining generation with deterministic verification increases mechanically checkable correctness [1],[3]. Critical analyses of LLM self-correction report that successful self-repair typically requires reliable external feedback or verifier signals [2]. Deterministic network-verification tools (header-space/Plankton/Batfish lineage) and GVR-like program-repair architectures provide established mechanisms to detect and sometimes correct syntactic and local-policy errors; however, deeper semantic correctness and cross-vendor subtleties remain challenging [4],[5],[6]. Security analyses of indirect prompt-injection emphasize the need for validation layers in LLM-integrated pipelines but also show that adaptive adversaries remain an unresolved threat [6]. This study differs by using a preregistered paired design with shared_initial_candidate semantics to isolate the marginal validator/repair effect on identical generated candidates.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 as a confirmatory paired design with N_pairs = 250, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, and primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The preregistration froze the single-repair policy, exclusion rules, and analysis procedures (exact McNemar two-sided and paired-bootstrap percentile CIs); preregistration SHA-256 = 7a984dbf7265c9a774eaf95c6c930dcf5f1e8845088bbc0e0855e3b4f1000ede.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics. For each intent exactly one initial model-generation call was produced and that identical candidate was reused for both episodes (baseline, guarded); no independent first-pass generation per condition was performed. Provider-call accounting reconcilied to hosted_model_call_event_count = 251 with stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1}, consistent with the shared_initial_candidate design.

Tasks and constraints. A deterministic task generator produced 250 constrained intent tasks. Each task encoded initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and a difficulty label. Tasks exercised realistic workflow constraints (e.g., make-before-break uplink switchover, paired-link atomic MTU changes, safe access transfer patterns). The full task manifest and representative payloads are archived in the evidence bundle.

Model, validator, and repair policy. All initial generations used gpt-5-mini. The guarded pipeline submitted the shared candidate to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implementing full_intent_constraint_validation: CLI parsing, required_sequence ordering checks, workflow-policy checks, and final_state snapshot comparison. If the validator returned valid=false the pipeline permitted up to one automated, template-driven repair (syntactic and ordering fixes only) and re-submitted the repaired candidate once. No human edits, multi-iteration repairs, or external live-protocol tests were permitted by design.

Inclusion, contamination, and analysis. Exclusion rules removed items that blocked deterministic verification (vendor-parser failures) or matched denylist/credential detectors. Contamination detectors flagged instruction-like embedded tokens; flagged items would be excluded from the primary analysis and treated in sensitivity analyses. No episodes were excluded or flagged in the executed confirmatory partition. The primary analysis used an exact two-sided McNemar on paired outcomes and a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729).
sections.results:
Execution and reconciled accounting. Execution completed the preregistered confirmatory partition with planned_episode_count = 500, completed_episode_count = 500, complete_pair_count = 250, and model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial_generation + 1 repair).

Primary outcomes. Validator-scored successes: baseline_success_count = 249 (baseline_success_rate = 0.996), guarded_success_count = 250 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). Observed paired contingency: n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The single discordant pair (baseline failed, guarded passed) corresponds to the lone exercised repair; the repair-conversion rate on the confirmatory partition = 1/250 = 0.004 (0.4%).

Statistical inference. Exact McNemar (two-sided) on discordant counts (n10 = 1, n01 = 0) returned p = 1.0. The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for guarded − baseline (10,000 resamples; seed = 1729) is [0.0, 0.012] (0 – 1.2 percentage points). These results and the contingency table are archived in the evidence bundle.

Validator diagnostics and repair. Representative validator traces show parsed_command_count and required_command_count equal to required_sequence length for passed episodes (example: task-000003 parsed_command_count = 6, required_command_count = 6). Only one automated repair call occurred and it converted the single failing baseline candidate into a guarded-pass; repair traces are archived.
sections.discussion:
Operational meaning. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics and the constrained synthetic/emulation partition used here, the marginal verifier-detected benefit of inserting a deterministic validator plus a single automated repair was small: initial gpt-5-mini candidates satisfied the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases and the guarded pipeline converted the single failing candidate via the single permitted repair. The paired-bootstrap CI upper bound (1.2 percentage points) provides an empirical bound on the possible verifier-improvement under these pipeline and task constraints.

Explanatory factors and interpretation. Artifact-grounded factors explaining the small gain include: (1) constrained task generation reduced ambiguity and favored well-formed CLI sequences, (2) the declared model produced highly consistent, syntactically well-formed sequences for these constrained intents, and (3) the deterministic validator measured mechanically verifiable properties and did not capture broader live-protocol behavioral correctness.

Power and assumptions. The preregistered power calculation assumed baseline ≈ 0.90 when selecting N_pairs = 250 to detect a 15 percentage-point absolute effect. The realized baseline pass rate (0.996) is substantially higher than assumed and thus reduces power to detect small absolute improvements; the paired-bootstrap CI is therefore a more informative practical bound here.

Threats to validity and scope. Internal validity depends on prompt templates, the single-repair policy, shared_initial_candidate semantics, and validator encoding. Construct validity: the deterministic validator checks syntax, ordering, and final_state snapshots but does not assert live protocol-level correctness. External validity: the confirmatory evidence covers only the synthetic/emulation partition; the preregistered sim-to-real/production-like confirmatory contrast was not executed and remains unreported. Security: adaptive prompt-injection and retrieval-based adversaries were not exercised.

Operational implications. These results show that in tightly constrained emulation-style tasks with a capable LLM the marginal verifier-detected improvement from a single repair may be limited. This should not be taken to imply validators or repair stages are unnecessary in broader or adversarial contexts: validator scope, multi-iteration repair, human escalation, and production heterogeneity can materially change outcomes.
sections.conclusion: We executed a sealed, preregistered paired experiment under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure the verifier-detected marginal benefit of deterministic validation plus one permitted automated repair on identical LLM-generated configuration candidates. In N = 250 constrained synthetic intent tasks, initial gpt-5-mini candidates passed the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases; the guarded pipeline converted the single failing candidate via the single permitted repair. Observed paired improvement = 0.4 percentage points (95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp]; p = 1.0). We explicitly disclose that the preregistered sim‑to‑real/production-like confirmatory contrast was not executed and that the executed confirmatory estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline on the synthetic/emulation partition only. Broader production, adversarial, multi-model, and multi-iteration repair evaluations remain necessary to establish generality. All execution and analysis artifacts referenced in this paper are archived in the evidence bundle described in the Disclosure Statement.

disclosure_statement:
Human role and autonomy boundary: After an autonomy lock required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track, the autonomous system performed literature search, study selection, preregistration freeze, prompt preservation, model calls, deterministic validation, permitted repair execution, analysis, drafting, peer-review, revision, and finalization without manual human editing of technical content. A human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and performed pre-lock infrastructure development; no human manually edited manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.

Models, tools, and manifest pointer: Declared model used for initial generations = gpt-5-mini (provider recorded as openai_responses). Deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Deterministic task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. The full execution and analysis manifests, raw responses, validator traces, repair traces, and artifact-hash manifest are archived; the archive's full manifest is available as the execution manifest: execution/execution_manifest.json (the archived bundle contains the complete per-artifact hashes and manifests referenced throughout this paper).

Preregistration and immutable prompt reference: Preregistration study id = study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 (preregistration SHA-256 = 7a984dbf7265c9a774eaf95c6c930dcf5f1e8845088bbc0e0855e3b4f1000ede). Immutable master prompt used to initiate the autonomous run is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Key reconciled numeric facts reported in the manuscript (model_calls_used = 251; stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1}; contingency counts n11=249/n10=1/n01=0/n00=0; bootstrap parameters: resamples = 10,000, seed = 1729) are reproducible from the archived manifests and the execution manifest named above.

Executed estimand and deviation disclosure: The preregistration included multiple partitions (synthetic/emulation, community, production-like) and a preregistered sim‑to‑real confirmatory contrast. Deviation disclosure: the preregistered sim-to-real/production-like confirmatory comparison was not executed in this run; the executed confirmatory estimand reported here is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline evaluated on the synthetic/emulation partition only (N_pairs = 250; shared_initial_candidate semantics).
limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed and remain exploratory.

Deterministic validator assessed mechanically verifiable properties (syntax and prescribed workflow sequences) but did not measure broader semantic or behavioral correctness (protocol dynamics, emergent interactions).
Single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and a single validator implementation were used; results do not establish multi-model or alternate-validator generality.
Only one automated repair attempt was permitted by design; multi-iteration repairs or human-in-the-loop escalation were not evaluated.
Adversarial and retrieval-based attacks (adaptive prompt-injection, vendor-targeted exploit vectors) and large-scale production heterogeneity were not exercised and remain open threats.
